focus: Whether upgrade-legacy's cost is spread across its 65 tests or concentrated
noveltyJustification: 4 of 6 findings are new counts and their reading; the sharding projection is a derivation from them and from iteration 1.
keyQuestions: Which of the 12 serial deep-loop files actually need serial execution, and what would shrink that group?
What sets the time of the cli lane's tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and can it be cut without dropping assertions?
Where do the roughly 300 s of import time in the spec-kit core lane come from, and which parts can be cut?
Do the ledger read-caching ideas (singleWriterReadCache, gateway rescans) buy measurable time, and what runtime risk do they carry?
Which remaining cuts still pay off on a smaller CI runner, and how should each be measured before it is claimed as a win?
answeredQuestions: What sets the time of the cli lane's tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and can it be cut without dropping assertions?
ruledOut: Cutting individual heavy tests: the top ten are only 36% of the calls
Trimming the sandbox copy to fund more shards: 35.8 MB once per shard is cheap
describe.concurrent inside one file: the shared sandbox would become the assertion
Raising the 180 s per-test timeouts: no test is timing out
sourcesQueried: measured: static per-test call count -> 65 tests, 105 calls, top-10 share 36%
